name: Deploy Rollback
description: Roll a Fabric deployment back to the last known-good state with fabio. Git is the source of truth, so a rollback is: revert the bad commit, re-deploy the reverted source with content-hash convergence, and verify. Covers Git-tracked items (deploy apply) and non-Git-tracked items (deployment-pipeline re-promote), plus the data caveat.
prerequisites: Authenticated via fabio auth login (or a CI service principal)
The source directory / repo whose Git history contains the last known-good commit
parameters.json (if the deployment uses environment-specific values)

steps.description: Identify the last known-good commit and the bad commit to revert.
steps.notes: Prefer git revert over reset so the rollback goes through the same PR review/approval gates as any change.

steps.description: Revert the bad commit (restores the previous item definitions).
steps.notes: git revert restores DEFINITIONS only — it does not restore data rows written by the bad release.

steps.description: Offline pre-flight on the reverted source (no API calls).
steps.notes: Also gate environment hygiene: fabio deploy validate --source ./fabric-items --pr-ready --expect-env prod.

steps.description: Preview the rollback changeset (what returns to the known-good state).
steps.notes: Review data.summary and data.destructive — a rollback can delete items that the bad release added (needs --delete-orphans; protected data types need --allow-delete-types).

steps.description: Re-deploy the reverted source; --verify audits convergence.
steps.notes: Content-hash diffing means only the items that changed back are touched. --verify adds a 'verification' block (converged:true expected).

steps.description: Confirm convergence — every item should now be Skip.
steps.notes: summary.create/update/delete == 0 means prod matches the known-good source.

steps.description: (Only if the workspace has non-Git-tracked items) Re-promote the previous stage's known-good version.
steps.notes: git revert does NOT touch Deployment-Pipeline-only items — see the item-tracking-categories best-practice.

steps.description: (If needed) Restore data state — a definition rollback does not undo data changes.
steps.notes: Re-run the ETL, or restore from a pre-deploy warehouse-snapshot / Lakehouse Delta time-travel.

tips: Snapshot data-bearing items BEFORE a risky deploy so a rollback has a data restore point: fabio warehouse-snapshot create ... (Warehouse); Lakehouses use Delta time-travel / OneLake restore.
A definition rollback (git revert + deploy apply) NEVER restores data rows — always plan the data recovery separately and warn the human.
Roll back only the affected items with --include-items or --git-diff instead of the whole workspace when the blast radius is known.
The rollback PR passes the same review/approval and branch-protection gates as any change — it is auditable like any other deployment.
See fabio context best-practices hotfix-rollback for the full playbook including the hotfix (forward-fix) flow and the production validation checklist.
